audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs appear omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.745 million fair-value liability at 2026-06-30, equal to approximately $0.12 per diluted share and 0.6%-0.9% of stated scenario equity values; disclosed contractual maximum was $14.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The current fair value of contingent acquisition consideration should be deducted as a debt-like claim in the equity bridge; settlement principal is not captured by interest expense retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company also has earn-out obligations related to recent acquisitions of up to $14.5 million based on the acquired business achieving specific revenue targets for up to a three-year post-acquisition period.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the latest filing reports a $3.745 million contingent-consideration liability while the bridge deducts none. The correction lowers every scenario by about $0.12 per share, leaving even the $19.81 bull value far below the $29.20 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion, although it should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $3.745 million 2026-06-30 fair-value liability from the bridge, confirm the remaining contractual maximum by acquisition, and retain fair-value remeasurement gains or losses only once in the OE reconciliation.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized sales commissions may be an unrecognized recurring cash investment
audit_findings.magnitude: Capitalized contract costs increased $4.2 million in 2025; with $12.633 million of amortization, implied additions were $16.833 million before any acquisition-related balance effects. The $4.2 million net increase equals 14.0% of the $30.1 million OE anchor.
audit_findings.mechanism: If the OE calculation starts from net income but neither replaces deferred-commission amortization with cash additions nor captures the additions through operating working-capital movements, OE and growth-funded cash generation are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Capitalized contract costs of $ 38.9 million and $ 34.7 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024 , respectively, are included under the caption other assets in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets, and amortization of deferred commissions is included in sales and marketing expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial recurring commission capitalization, but the record does not show whether each OE calculation already captures it through cash-flow working-capital adjustments. If omitted, the 2025 net cash-investment gap alone is large relative to the anchor and reasonably capable of materially reducing the DCF. This is therefore an unresolved but potentially material calculation issue, not a demonstrated OE error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each historical OE year to the deferred-commission roll-forward and cash-flow statement, separating acquisition balances from cash additions; then rerun all scenarios with amortization added back and cash additions deducted where those cash flows are not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor contains almost none of the acquired businesses' annual earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 pro formas indicate Virsys12 reduced net income by approximately $0.302 million and MissionCare increased it by approximately $1.699 million, a computed combined indication of positive $1.397 million, equal to 4.6% of the $30.1 million OE anchor; OE-specific effect remains unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Using FY2025 as-filed OE omits most post-acquisition annual earnings and reinvestment while the latest bridge and share count represent the post-acquisition equity claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating results of the acquired operations of Virsys12 and MissionCare comprised approximately 0.5% of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed pro formas indicate mixed target results and only a roughly $1.4 million combined net-income effect. Even treating that amount as proportional to OE would imply only about a 4.6% valuation increase, insufficient to close the gap between the $19.81 bull value and the $29.20 price. The actual owner-earnings contribution is not established, so the anchor should still be superseded when full-year evidence is available.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Virsys12 and MissionCare standalone post-close cash earnings, capitalized commissions, and maintenance investment; replace the partial-year anchor with the first filed full-year OE without introducing management forecasts.

audit_findings.title: Finite sublease income is embedded in an otherwise perpetual earnings stream
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $3.2 million of annual sublease income through October 2031 versus $3.9 million of 2025 operating-lease expense; post-2031 replacement occupancy cost is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Sublease income raises current OE and is otherwise carried through growth and terminal value, but the associated head-lease expense also expires in October 2031 and future replacement occupancy expense is unknown.
audit_findings.evidence: The sublease commenced in April 2025 and will expire in October 2031.
audit_findings.explanation: The finite income and common expiration date are demonstrated. Perpetuating the $3.2 million income alone would overstate value, while removing it without also removing the head-lease cost could understate value. Because the required post-expiration premises and occupancy cost are absent, the record cannot establish either the net direction or materiality of the terminal adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Build a lease schedule through October 2031 showing head-lease expense and sublease receipts, estimate supportable replacement occupancy cost from filed operational evidence, and rerun the terminal period using only normalized net occupancy expense.

audit_findings.title: Non-marketable investments appear absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.0 million carrying amount at 2026-06-30, approximately $0.10 per diluted share and 0.5%-0.7% of stated scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: If classified as non-operating, the investments should be added in the equity bridge while related equity-method losses and valuation effects are removed consistently from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate carrying amount of non-marketable equity investments accounted for using the measurement alternative for equity investments that do not have readily determinable fair values was $ 1.5 million for both the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , which the Company evaluates for impairment at each reporting period, and are classified in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates at least $3.0 million of measurement-alternative investments while stakes_net is zero. At carrying value, adding them changes each scenario by only about $0.10 per share and cannot alter the conclusion relative to the $29.20 market price. Any additional equity-method investment value is not quantified by the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the 2026-06-30 carrying and realizable values of measurement-alternative and equity-method investments, classify each as operating or non-operating, add the supportable non-operating amount to the bridge, and treat its earnings or losses consistently in OE.
